priorStories.headline: Thanksgiving storm leaves 900,000 customers without power
priorStories.body:
A Thanksgiving storm brought strong winds, coastal flooding and widespread power outages to the East Coast. Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland and Virginia were among the hardest-hit states.

More than 908,000 utility customers nationwide were without electricity at 9:56 p.m. Eastern, down from 961,000 at 7:30 p.m., Reuters reported, citing PowerOutage.us. FlightAware recorded 454 cancellations and 2,411 delays for U.S.-related flights Thursday.

candidates.summary: FAO and the World Food Programme released a report identifying 16 hunger hotspots where acute food insecurity could worsen between December 2026 and May 2027, up from 13 in June. Northern Nigeria, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Yemen were classified as the areas of highest concern. New additions included Southern Africa, the Central American Dry Corridor, northeastern Uganda and Chad. The agencies cited conflict, El Niño and funding constraints and called for urgent humanitarian assistance and safe access.
candidates.title: FAO and WFP identify 16 hunger hotspots in new early-warning report

candidates.summary: India's federal government urged states to sign purchase contracts for 41 gigawatts of clean-energy capacity without buyers. Speaking at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi, minister Shripad Naik also called for more battery-storage contracts, earlier demand planning and faster land-acquisition payments for transmission projects. Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said evening demand had strained the system in September and October despite surplus daytime solar generation. The remarks were requests to states, not announcements that contracts had been signed.
candidates.title: India urges states to contract for 41 GW of clean-energy capacity

candidates.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal told an industry conference that the process for completing an India-US trade agreement was taking shape and that the deal was nearing completion. His remarks followed a Wednesday US proposal to cap tariffs on Indian imports at 17% if an agreement was reached, rather than raise them to 25%. Goyal's statement did not announce a signed agreement or an effective tariff change.
candidates.title: Goyal says India-US trade negotiations are nearing completion

candidates.summary: The board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS, the group's Norwegian operating subsidiary, resolved on November 27 to file a bankruptcy petition with Agder District Court after efforts to secure sufficient short-term funding failed. Norse said all flights were cancelled and ticket sales discontinued. The listed parent, Norse Atlantic ASA, and other group companies are not included in the filing. Management said it was seeking a solution for the remaining business, including the UK subsidiary.
candidates.title: Norse's Norwegian operating subsidiary resolves to file for bankruptcy

sources.name: Norse Atlantic stock exchange announcement via Cision

candidates.summary: Deutsche Börse announced that the European Commission had unconditionally cleared its proposed acquisition of Allfunds following an initial merger review. The transaction has not completed: further supervisory clearances and approval of the scheme of arrangement by the competent English court remain outstanding.
candidates.title: European Commission clears Deutsche Börse's proposed Allfunds acquisition

sources.name: Deutsche Börse regulatory announcement via EQS News

candidates.summary: CPTPP ministers meeting in Hanoi decided to establish accession working groups for the United Arab Emirates, Indonesia and the Philippines, following preparatory discussions begun in June. This starts accession negotiations rather than granting membership. The joint statement also recorded Costa Rica's decision not to sign its accession protocol at this meeting and established an interim CPTPP support office in Japan to begin work in 2027.
candidates.title: CPTPP opens accession negotiations with UAE, Indonesia and Philippines
candidates.geography: Vietnam; United Arab Emirates; Indonesia; Philippines; Pacific Rim

sources.name: CPTPP joint ministerial statement via UK government

candidates.summary: Ofcom revoked Lualua TV licence holder Shells for Media Productions Limited's UK broadcast licence with immediate effect, concluding it was not fit and proper to hold one. The regulator cited online material it found promoted proscribed terrorist organisations and contained unchallenged antisemitic hate speech, alongside a lack of transparency during its investigation. Lualua was not currently broadcasting under the licence on regulated UK television platforms. Revocation prevents broadcasting under that licence on those platforms but does not prevent its online livestream.
candidates.title: Ofcom revokes Lualua TV's UK broadcast licence

candidates.summary: Entain announced a preliminary agreement between its Australian subsidiary and AUSTRAC proposing a civil penalty of A$185 million plus costs to resolve anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism-financing proceedings. The proceedings concern contraventions between December 2018 and August 2024. The proposed agreed facts, admissions and penalty remain subject to final Entain board and AUSTRAC approval, as well as Federal Court approval; no final court-approved settlement was announced.
candidates.title: Entain announces preliminary A$185 million agreement in Australian compliance case

sources.name: Entain regulatory announcement via London South East

candidates.summary: BAE Systems said a joint combat-vehicle order from Finland, Sweden, Norway, Lithuania and the Netherlands totals $6 billion. Reuters reported that the countries signed the joint procurement in Stockholm on Friday, following Finland's announcement on Thursday that they would buy more than 430 CV90 vehicles. The vehicles are made by BAE Systems Hägglunds in Sweden.
candidates.title: Five European countries sign $6 billion joint CV90 procurement

candidates.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada upheld Quebec's Act respecting the laicity of the State, commonly called Bill 21, except for a provision infringing Charter democratic rights insofar as it applies to members of Quebec's National Assembly. The court confirmed that Quebec had validly invoked constitutional override clauses. It also held that invoking the override power does not prevent courts from declaring legislation inconsistent with overridden Charter provisions, but made no such declaration in this case.
candidates.title: Canada's Supreme Court upholds most of Quebec's secularism law

sources.name: Supreme Court of Canada judgment announcement
Supreme Court of Canada case summary

candidates.summary: WSSC Water lifted its voluntary essential-water-use-only request at 8:30 a.m. for 1.9 million customers in Montgomery and Prince George's counties. The utility said both filtration plants were producing safe drinking water and its treatment and distribution system was operating normally after power disruptions from the previous day's storm diminished.
candidates.title: Maryland utility lifts storm-related water conservation request for 1.9 million customers

candidates.summary: Britain's government confirmed that some Department for Work and Pensions online services had been taken offline as a precaution following a cyber incident. It said regular benefit and pension payments were unaffected and investigators were working with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre. Sky News reported that the problem was first identified Thursday evening; the nature of the incident had not been established publicly.
candidates.title: UK government confirms DWP online services taken offline after cyber incident

sources.name: Sky News, including DWP spokesperson statement

candidates.summary: S&P Global Ratings raised South Africa's long-term foreign-currency sovereign rating to BB+ from BB on November 27 and assigned a stable outlook. The agency cited improving fiscal performance and continued fiscal consolidation despite economic pressures from the Middle East conflict.
candidates.title: S&P upgrades South Africa's sovereign credit rating to BB+

candidates.summary: S&P Global Ratings changed France's sovereign credit outlook from stable to negative on November 27 while affirming its A+/A-1 ratings. The agency cited weak growth, higher interest costs and political polarization that could impede deficit reduction. The decision changed the outlook, not the credit rating itself.
candidates.title: S&P changes France's credit outlook to negative while affirming ratings

candidates.summary: Reuters reported on November 27, citing people familiar with the matter, that hackers had breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform. Sources said discovery during upgrade work within roughly the preceding month disrupted application migrations and updates. The breach and discovery were not established as November 27 events; this candidate records their public disclosure. Reuters could not establish responsibility, the intrusion's full scope or whether data was stolen. The Air Force declined to discuss specific systems' security or operational status.
candidates.title: Reuters discloses reported breach of US Air Force Cloud One platform

candidates.summary: Britain's Department for Work and Pensions confirmed on November 27 that it had taken some online services offline as a precaution following a cyber incident; services appeared to remain offline Friday evening. The department said regular benefit and pension payments were unaffected and customers directly affected by the incident would not face sanctions. Previously processed sanctions remained applicable. Investigators were working with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre. The government had not publicly established the cause; minister Pat McFadden said there was no evidence so far that personal details had been compromised.
candidates.title: DWP says customers affected by cyber-related service outage will not face sanctions

sources.name: Sky News, including DWP spokesperson statement
Press Association via LBC, including DWP statement
The Guardian, reporting Pat McFadden's statement
